title: བར་དོ་ཐོས་གྲོལ་ཆེན་མོ།
titleEn: The Tibetan Book of the Dead — The bardo of the wrathful deities begins: why it is hard to recognise, and who is freed
part: 9 · The bardo of the wrathful deities begins: why it is hard to recognise, and who is freed
draftNote: Read from one blockprint at the resolution of an online scan; doubtful places are marked in the notes, and the text has not yet been collated with other prints.
source: Zab chos zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol las: Khro bo'i bar do 'char tshul bstan pa (the wrathful deities), pages 81–90 of the reproduction, from an undated Tibetan blockprint of the Thos grol cycle reproduced by the Buddhist Digital Resource Center as W23710 (text ga), read from the page images. It is a traditional blockprint, so no modern editor's work is involved. Two transcriptions found online, one of this print and one of another, were used to check the reading and are not the text. The page gives the print's wording and spelling. Three things are ours: the spaces between words, which Tibetan does not write; the line-end abbreviations, written out; and clear misprints corrected, each named in its note. Where another print reads differently in a way that matters, the note says so. Letters: the Wylie system (Extended Wylie for the Sanskrit words). Pronunciation: the reading style of central Tibet in the THL Simplified Phonetic Transcription (Germano and Tournadre, 2003), produced by rule from the spelling; a living reader's pronunciation will differ in places. The translation is new, made from the Tibetan. Still to do: the text has been read from one print at the resolution of an online scan, and doubtful places are marked in the notes; it has not been collated with the other blockprints.

sentences.l: Wrathful-ones' between, dawning-manner showing, is-here.
sentences.i: Here is the showing of how the bardo of the wrathful deities dawns.
sentences.n: The title leaf of text ga, the third text of the volume and the second part of the Great Liberation through Hearing; the letter ga stands in the top margin. Like the title of text kha in the pilot, it is one phrase closed by bzhugs so, 'is present', the respectful way a title page says 'here is'. khro bo, 'wrathful one' (khro, 'wrath'), the wrathful forms of the deities, against the zhi ba, 'peaceful', of the parts before. 'char tshul, 'the way of dawning' (tshul, 'manner, way'); bstan pa, 'showing, teaching', the past stem of ston, 'to show', made a noun with -pa. The print runs bar do and 'char together with no tsheg (བར་དོའཆར), here divided; it does the same in the next line.

sentences.l: Them-at, stages according-to, face-introduced-because: one at not met though, one at met, and, freedom obtaining, as-for, measure-to without-ly arises.
sentences.i: and because the dead were pointed out at each in turn, those who did not recognise at one recognised at another and were freed; those who gained freedom so are beyond counting.
sentences.n: The print has དེ་ཡ (de ya), a misprint for དེ་ལ (de la), corrected here: the letter was compared with other ya and la on the page, and only de la, 'at them, to them', gives sense, and the other recension has de rnams la, 'at those'; the reading is fairly but not wholly sure. rim pa bzhin du, 'stage by stage, in order'. ngo sprad pas, 'because they were pointed out' (ngo sprad, the past of ngo sprod, 'point out', with -pa and -s 'by, because'). ngo and thob are both doubtful on the image ([?]): a naro may be hidden under the line above, which would give other letters; ngo sprad and thob pa are the words the sense needs. cig la ma 'phrod kyang gcig la 'phrod, 'though it is not met at one, it is met at another': ngo 'phrod, 'the face meets', is recognition, though the print has 'phrod alone both times, where the other recension has ngo ma 'phrod and ngo 'phrod; cig and gcig, 'one', are the same word in two spellings. The print writes la ma as one sign in mid-line (ལམ), and runs la and 'phrod together at the next line join; both are written out here. dpag tu med par 'byung, 'arise beyond measure'; 'byung ngo, with the sentence-ending -o, written ngo after -ng.

sentences.l: Thus freedom many-ly arose though: beings, as-for, numbers many; bad-deeds, as-for, force great; wrongs-obscurations, as-for, dense-thick; habitual-tendencies, as-for, duration long; ignorance's delusion-wheel this at, exhausting is-not and, lessening at(?) is-not, because:
sentences.i: Yet though many were freed in this way, beings are countless, bad karma is strong, wrongdoing and obscuration are thick, habitual tendencies are long-standing, and this delusive wheel of ignorance never runs out and never grows less. So
sentences.n: Four short clauses, each with ni, 'as for', set out why so many remain: sems can ni grangs mang, 'beings, their numbers are many'; las ngan ni tshan che, 'bad karma, its force is great' (tshan che, 'strong'); sdig sgrib ni lhun stug, 'wrongs and obscurations are dense' (sdig, 'wrongdoing'; sgrib, 'obscuration'; lhun stug, 'massive, thick'); bag chags ni yun ring, 'habitual tendencies are of long duration'. The print sets the ༔ after stug and ring apart from the word, with no tsheg. mang du[?] byung: on the image one u-loop serves both du and the bya below it, so du is not sure. byung is the past stem, 'arose, have been', where the other recension has the present 'byung. ma rig 'khrul 'khor: 'khrul 'khor is a machine or turning device, and it carries both 'khrul, 'delusion', and 'khor, 'turning, saṃsāra': 'the delusive wheel of ignorance'. zad pa med, 'there is no running out'; 'phri ba la[?] med, 'there is no lessening': the la is doubtful, is not in the other recension, and makes the phrase awkward; it is translated as if absent. med pas, 'because there is not', runs on into the next sentence.

sentences.l: That also: peaceful's deity-host and; knowledge-holders sky-goers' deity-host's welcoming passed's after-at, blood-drinking wrathful-ones' deity-host blazing fifty-and-eight; above's peaceful's deity-host, state transformed, and(?), dawning come-because, above with not alike, and:
sentences.i: After the welcome of the hosts of peaceful deities and of the knowledge-holders and sky-goers has passed, the fifty-eight blazing blood-drinking wrathful deities come. They are the peaceful deities of before, changed in state, who now dawn, and so they are not like what went before.
sentences.n: khrag 'thung, 'blood-drinker' (khrag, 'blood'; 'thung, 'to drink'; Sanskrit heruka), the name of the wrathful deities; 'bar ba, 'blazing'. lnga bcu rtsa brgyad, 'fifty-eight': lnga bcu, 'fifty', and rtsa, which joins the units to the tens, brgyad, 'eight'. bsu ba 'das pa'i 'og tu, 'after the welcoming has passed': the knowledge-holders and sky-goers came to welcome the dead in 007 and 008. The other recension has rig 'dzin mkha' 'gro'i bsun ma 'das pa'i 'og tu, without lha tshogs kyi and with bsun ma for bsu ba. 'dzin[?] in rig 'dzin is squeezed against the frame on the image and not sure, but the word is the one the sense needs; the print runs it and mkha' together with no tsheg, here divided. gnas bsgyur, 'changed in state' (gnas, 'place, state'; bsgyur, the past stem of sgyur, 'to change, transform'), where the other recension has gnas 'gyur nas, 'having changed'. de after bsgyur is taken as the clause link 'and', though after -r it is usually written te; it could also be 'that'. 'char du 'ong, 'come to dawn'; -bas, 'because'. gong dang mi 'dra, 'not like before': dang, 'with', after 'dra, 'to be alike'. The other recension ends the sentence at 'ong ngo and goes on with da ni ... 'dir.

sentences.l: This, as-for, wrathful-ones' between is-because: fear, fright, terror, three's power-into go, and: face-meeting also difficult-ly goes.
sentences.i: Because this is the bardo of the wrathful deities, the dead fall into the power of fear, fright and terror, and recognition grows harder.
sentences.n: 'jigs skrag dngangs gsum, 'the three, fear, fright and terror', three words for one thing, said again below as dngangs skrag 'jigs gsum; dngangs is the print's spelling of sngangs, 'to be terrified'. dbang du 'gro, 'go into the power (of)'. dka' ru 'gro, 'go to difficulty, become hard': ru, 'to, into', after a word ending in a vowel; 'gro'o, 'goes', with the sentence-ending -'o after a vowel. The print runs 'di and ni together at the page end (འདིནི) and ni and khro across the page join; here divided.

sentences.l: Knowing own-power not obtains, fainting circle-whole-ly comes, and:
sentences.i: Awareness gets no command of itself, and fainting comes over it again and again;
sentences.n: The print has བརྒྱལ་བབཁོར (brgyal ba ba khor, the second ba with no tsheg), a misprint for བརྒྱལ་བ་ཁོར (brgyal ba khor), corrected here: the letter ba is set twice, once as the last syllable of brgyal ba, 'fainting, swoon', and again before khor; the correction is fairly but not wholly sure. rang dbang, 'own power, control of oneself'; mi thob, 'does not get', with mi, the 'not' of the present. khor yug tu, 'all round, without a break' (khor yug, 'circumference, the whole round'); the sense, swoon upon swoon, is taken from the words and is not sure. The other recension has mi thob par brgyal te, de kho ra khor yug tu 'ong, 'faints without gaining command, and that very state comes all round'; the print has neither par nor te de kho ra. The print also runs thob and brgyal together at the line join, here divided.

sentences.n: 'dul ba, 'discipline' (Sanskrit vinaya), the monastic code; 'dul ba 'dzin pa, 'one who holds the discipline'; mkhan po, 'abbot', the senior monk who gives ordination. mtshan nyid, 'defining characteristic', is the name for the study of philosophy by definitions and debate; mtshan nyid kyi ston pa, 'a teacher of philosophy'. sentences.i: This is how it works: in the human world one has meditated on these blood-drinking deities in their sādhanas, made them offerings and praises, or even only seen their images painted or moulded in relief, and by that alone, when the images dawn here, one recognises them and is freed. sentences.i: That is because in their lifetime the secret mantra found no room in their minds, they reviled and disparaged it, and they had no acquaintance with its deities; so when those deities dawn in the bardo, they do not recognise them.

sentences.n: de'i phyir, 'for that reason, therefore'; the other recension has des. sentences.i: A mantrin, even the lowest of the low, however coarse, undisciplined and unlearned his conduct may seem for the time being, however unseemly and out of keeping with custom, and even if he cannot put the secret mantra into practice, need only have formed no wrong views of it, have no doubt, and have devotion to it, to be freed at this point.
sentences.n: gsang sngags pa, 'mantrin', a follower of the secret mantra, often a lay tantric. na'ang is a contraction of na yang, 'even if'. 'phral du, 'for the moment, outwardly'. spyod lam, 'conduct, behaviour'; rtsing pa, 'coarse'; mi btsun pa, 'undisciplined, undignified' (btsun pa, 'disciplined, reverend'); tshul dang mi mthun pa, 'not in agreement with propriety'. ji ltar 'dug kyang, 'however it may seem'. des, 'by him', marks the doer of blang, 'to take', the future stem of len: nyams su blang ma thub, 'could not put into practice'. log lta, 'wrong view'; the tshom, 'doubt'; mos pa, 'devotion'. tsam kyang, 'even merely'. sentences.l: That's sign-as: sky haze-pure and; rainbow and light-into dissolving and; flowers' rain and; incense's scent and; sky-in music-as(?) sound, rays(?) and; bone-relics and pearl-relics and; images and-so-on come-forth, as-for, that's sign is.
sentences.i: As signs of it, the sky is clear and without haze, there is dissolving into rainbow and light, a rain of flowers, the scent of incense, music and rays of light in the sky, and bone relics, pearl relics, images and the like appear: these are its signs.
sentences.n: The print has ནམ་མཁར (nam mkhar), a misprint for ནམ་མཁའ (nam mkha'), corrected here: the letter is clearly the open ར, set beside the closed འ of mkha' earlier in the same line, and nam mkha', 'sky', is the only word. rtags[?] su: the print writes rtag at the line end, squeezed against the frame and not sure, with su on the next line; rtags su, 'as a sign', is written out. g.ya' dag pa, 'clean of haze' (g.ya', 'haze, tarnish'). 'ja' dang 'od du thim pa, 'dissolving into rainbow and light': who or what dissolves is not said. me tog gi char, 'a rain of flowers'; spos kyi dri, 'the scent of incense'. rol mor sgra is kept as printed: rol mo is 'music', and rol mor, 'as music', is awkward; the other recension has rol mo'i, 'of music'. The print may have ར for འ here as in mkhar, but rol mo'i would also need a gi-gu, so it is not corrected; the sense is taken as 'the sound of music'. zer[?], 'rays', is very doubtful: one tall stack stands at the line end with no clear vowel, and is read zer because the other recension has sgra dang zer dang, 'sounds and rays'; the print has no dang after sgra. The print also has a stray tsheg in dang across the line join (ད་ང), here removed. byon pa, 'having come forth', the respectful past.

sentences.i: Therefore for the holders of the discipline, for philosophers, for mantrins whose commitments are broken, and for all ordinary people, there is no doing without this Great Liberation through Hearing.
sentences.n: dam tshig nyams pa'i sngags pa, 'a mantrin whose commitments (dam tshig, Sanskrit samaya) are broken'. X med pa'i thabs med, 'there is no way of being without X': it cannot be done without. The print runs dam and tshig together across the page join and its opening ornament, here divided. This line, 89.1, is a short one, closed by an empty framed box.

sentences.i: Great meditators who practise the Great Perfection, the Great Seal and the like recognise the clear light in the bardo of the moment of death and attain the body of truth, so they all, without exception, have no need of this Liberation through Hearing being read.
sentences.n: rdzogs chen, 'great perfection' (Dzogchen), the highest teaching of the Nyingma school, and rdzogs chen pa, one who practises it; phyag rgya chen po, 'the Great Seal' (008). sgom chen, 'great meditator', a meditator who has given his life to it; dag, plural. chos sku thob par 'gyur bas, 'because they come to attain the body of truth'; the print runs 'gyur and bas together at the line join, here divided. klog, 'to read (aloud)', the present stem, as in the pilot (klog par bya), where the other recension has klag; and the print has thos grol 'di without chen mo, where the other recension has thos grol chen mo 'di. sha stag, 'nothing but, every one' (008); 'ong ngo, 'they come to be'.

sentences.l: Becoming's in-the-between recognition seized, then, emanation-body obtaining and; others (plural) by(?) high-realms-in being-born, and: teaching this with met, then, birth later formed(?) and practising's karmic-residue there-is-because:
sentences.i: In the bardo of becoming, those who recognise attain the body of emanation; and others are born in the higher realms, because, having met this teaching, they have the karmic residue to practise it in a later birth.
sentences.n: srid pa'i bar do, 'the bardo of becoming', in which a new birth is sought; it is the subject of text ja. sprul sku, 'the body of emanation'. gzhan dag kas[?] is a phrase the other recension does not have, and two of its letters are doubtful: gzhan dag, 'others', is clear, then a ka and a sa-like letter crushed against the frame. A word such as gzhan dag kyang, 'others, too', would fit the sense, but no ya-btags or nga is seen, so the letters stand as read; kas is taken as ka with -s, the ending that marks a doer, though skye, 'to be born', does not usually take one; the reading is uncertain. The other recension has gnas, 'abodes', at this point (sprul sku thob pa dang gnas mtho rus su skyes te), so the crushed letters may also stand for gnas: 'others are born in the high abodes'. mtho ris, 'the high realms', the births of gods and humans. chags[?] is doubtful and is another word not in the other recension: chags is 'to come into being, take shape' (also 'to be attached'), and the phrase is taken as 'when the later birth takes shape, to practise'; the sense of chags la here is not sure. las 'phro, 'karmic residue', as in the parts before. The print adds a second group, 'others': in the other recension those who attain the body of emanation are themselves born in the high abodes, while the print gives that birth to others. The print has no tsheg before the ༔ of dang.

sentences.l: That's because: Hearing-Liberation Great this, as-for: not meditating-ly buddha-becoming's teaching, hearing merely by freedom obtaining's teaching; great-wrongdoers secret-path onto leading's teaching; instant one by distinction dividing's teaching; instant one by perfect-buddha-becoming's teaching profound is, and:
sentences.i: Therefore this Great Liberation through Hearing is the teaching by which one becomes a buddha without meditating, the teaching that frees by hearing alone, the teaching that leads great wrongdoers onto the secret path, the teaching that makes the difference in a single instant, the profound teaching by which one becomes a perfect buddha in a single instant;
sentences.n: A list of names for the teaching, each ending in chos, 'teaching', with ༔ after each but the first; without that ༔ the first two could also be read as one, 'the teaching by which one is freed merely by hearing the teaching of becoming a buddha without meditating'. The other recension has the ༔ there (ma sgom par sangs rgyas pa'i chos༔), which supports two names. ma bsgom par, 'without meditating' (bsgom, the future stem of sgom); sangs[?] is blotted on the image, though sangs rgyas, 'buddha', is not in doubt. thos pa tsam gyis, 'by merely hearing'. sdig po che, 'great wrongdoer'; gsang lam, 'the secret path', where the other recension has gseb lam, 'the hidden path'; 'khrid, 'to lead'. skad cig gcig gis, 'in a single instant'. bye brag phyed, 'to divide the difference', to make the decisive distinction, between saṃsāra and freedom. rdzogs sangs rgyas, 'perfectly awakened'. The print runs par and sangs together across the page join, and pa'i and chos at the next line join; both are divided here.

sentences.l: This-by reached's beings, bad-destinies-to gone, not possible.
sentences.i: no being whom it has reached can go to the lower realms.
sentences.n: 'dis, 'by this', with the -s that marks the doer. sleb pa'i sems can, 'the beings reached': sleb, 'to arrive, reach', the beings to whom the teaching comes. song ba, 'having gone'. mi srid do, 'it is not possible'. The next part begins on the same line, with 'di dang.

glossary.ཀས: kas — a doubtful reading of this print (ka + -s?) after gzhan dag 'others': perhaps for kyang 'too', or for gnas 'abodes' (gzhan dag gnas mtho ris su 'others in the high abodes'); the sense is not sure
glossary.ཀྱང: kyang — also, even, though (the form of yang after g, d, b, s)
glossary.ཀྱི: kyi — of (the form used after d, b, s; also gyi, gi, -'i, yi) · in this print perhaps also written where kyis 'by' is meant (khyod kyi gong du, read as khyod kyis)
glossary.ཁོ་ནས: kho nas — by that alone, only (kho na 'only' + -s 'by')
glossary.ཁོར་ཡུག་ཏུ: khor yug tu — all round, without a break (khor yug 'circumference, the whole round' + -tu); of a recurring state, 'again and again'
glossary.ཁྲག་འཐུང: khrag 'thung — blood-drinker, blood-drinking: the name of the wrathful deities (khrag 'blood' + 'thung, the present stem of 'to drink', past 'thungs; Sanskrit heruka)
glossary.ཁྲོ་བོའི: khro bo'i — of the wrathful ones, wrathful (khro bo 'wrathful one' + -'i 'of')
glossary.གཅིག: gcig — one; a, a certain · perhaps 'together, at once' (as gcig 'one' in 'od drug kyang gcig 'char du 'ong 'the six lights also dawn together'); the sense is not sure
glossary.གཉིས་སུ: gnyis su — into two, as two (gnyis 'two' + -su): gnyis su med par 'without being two, non-dually'
glossary.གདན་དྲངས་པར: gdan drangs par — to be invited, to be escorted with honour (gdan 'seat' + drangs, the past stem of 'dren 'lead', + -pa + -r 'into'): gdan drangs par 'gyur 'will be escorted'
glossary.གདུང: gdung — bone relic, the bones left after cremation (gdung, the respectful word for 'bones')
glossary.གནད: gnad — vital point, key point (gnad): the place where a thing is decided, like a pressure point on the body
glossary.གནས: gnas — to remain, to stay; a place · state, condition (gnas bsgyur 'changed in state')
glossary.གཡང: g.yang — abyss, precipice (g.yang; usually g.yang sa)
glossary.གཡའ: g.ya' — haze, cloudiness, a stain on the sky (g.ya')
glossary.གཤེ་སྐུར: gshe skur — reviling and disparaging (gshe 'to revile, scold' + skur 'to disparage')
glossary.གསང་ལམ: gsang lam — secret path, the path of the tantras (gsang 'secret' + lam 'path')
glossary.གསང་སྔགས: gsang sngags — secret mantra, the tantric teaching (gsang 'secret' + sngags 'mantra'; Sanskrit guhyamantra)
glossary.གསང་སྔགས་པ: gsang sngags pa — mantrin, follower of the secret mantra (gsang sngags + -pa)
glossary.གསོན་པོའི: gson po'i — of the living, alive (gson po 'alive' + -'i 'of')
glossary.གི: gi — of (the form used after g, ng); in this print also written where gis 'by' is meant · after a verb: 'and', running on to what follows ('ong gi 'comes, and')
glossary.གིས: gis — by (the form used after g, ng) · after a verb: 'and', running on to what follows, as gi does ('ong gis 'comes, and')
glossary.གོང: gong — above, before, earlier (gong 'above'); gong gi 'the one above'
glossary.གྱི: gyi — of (the form used after n, m, r, l)
glossary.གྱིས: gyis — do! (imperative of byed 'to do'); spelled the same as gyis 'by' · by (the 'by' ending as a free word after n, m, r, l): las bzang ngan gyis 'by good or bad karma'
glossary.གྲངས: grangs — number, count (grangs): grangs mang 'many in number'
glossary.གྲོངས་པའི: grongs pa'i — of one who has died, at death (grongs pa 'to die', respectful, + -'i 'of'): grongs pa'i tshe 'at the time of death'
glossary.གྲོལ་བ: grol ba — being freed, liberation (grol + ba, which makes a verb into a noun)
glossary.གྲོལ་བར: grol bar — to be freed, that one will be freed (grol ba + -r)
glossary.ངན་སོང: ngan song — bad destiny, lower realm (ngan 'bad' + song 'gone')
glossary.ངན་སོང་དུ: ngan song du — into the lower realms, bad destinies (ngan song 'bad going' + -du 'into')
glossary.ངོ: ngo — face; the nature or identity of a thing
glossary.ངོ་སྤྲད: ngo sprad — pointing out, face-introduction (ngo sprad, past of ngo sprod 'point out')
glossary.ངོ་སྤྲད་པས: ngo sprad pas — by being pointed out (ngo sprad 'point out' + -pa + -s 'by')
glossary.ངོས: ngos — face, recognition (ngos 'face, side'); ngos zin 'recognise'
glossary.ཅིག: cig — one, a (gcig written without its prefix g-)
glossary.ཅིང: cing — and, while (links two verbs; also shing, zhing)
glossary.ཅིས་ཀྱང: cis kyang — by all means, in any case (ci 'what' + -s 'by' + kyang 'even')
glossary.ཅུང་ཟད: cung zad — a little, somewhat (cung zad)
glossary.ཆགས: chags — to be attached, attachment (chags) · to come into being, to take shape (chags): skye ba phyi ma chags 'a later birth takes shape'; the sense is not sure
glossary.ཆད: chad — to stop, to be cut off
glossary.ཆར: char — rain (char): me tog gi char 'a rain of flowers'
glossary.ཆེ་བའི: che ba'i — of the greater, senior (che ba 'great' + -'i 'of') · of great, in whom … is great (sdig sgrib che ba'i gang zag 'persons of heavy sinful obscurations')
glossary.ཆེན་མོ: chen mo — great (chen 'big', with the feminine ending often used in titles)
glossary.ཆོས: chos — thing, phenomenon; the teaching (Sanskrit dharma) · reality, what is true (chos): chos kyi rang sgra 'the own sound of reality'
glossary.ཆོས་ཉིད: chos nyid — reality itself, the true nature of things (chos 'thing' + nyid 'itself'; Sanskrit dharmatā)
glossary.ཆོས་སྐུ: chos sku — the body of truth, a buddha as reality itself, without form (chos + sku 'body'; Sanskrit dharmakāya)
glossary.ཆོས་སྤྱོད: chos spyod — religious practice, living by the teaching (chos 'teaching' + spyod 'practice')
glossary.ཇི་ལྟར: ji ltar — however, in what way (ji 'what' + ltar 'like')
glossary.ཉམས་པའི: nyams pa'i — of the broken, that is spoiled (nyams pa 'to be damaged, to lapse' + -'i 'of'): dam tshig nyams pa'i 'whose commitments are broken'
glossary.ཉམས་ལེན: nyams len — practice, taking into experience (nyams 'experience' + len 'take')
glossary.ཉམས་སུ་བླང: nyams su blang — to put into practice, to take into experience (nyams su 'into experience' + blang, the future stem of len 'take': len / blangs / blang / longs)
glossary.ཉམས་སུ་བླངས་པ: nyams su blangs pa — practised, having put into practice (nyams su 'into experience' + blangs, the past stem of len 'take', + -pa)
glossary.ཏེ: te — and, and so: links a verb to what follows (te, the form of ste after n, r, l; this print also writes it after other letters)
glossary.ཐ་ན: tha na — even, at the least (tha 'end' + na 'at')
glossary.ཐ་མ: tha ma — lowest, last (tha ma): tha ma'i yang tha ma 'the lowest even of the lowest'
glossary.ཐ་མའི: tha ma'i — of the lowest (tha ma 'lowest, last' + -'i 'of')
glossary.ཐ་མལ་པ: tha mal pa — ordinary, common one (tha mal pa)
glossary.ཐིམ: thim — to dissolve, to be absorbed (thim)
glossary.ཐིམ་པ: thim pa — dissolving, sinking in (thim + pa)
glossary.ཐུབ: thub — able (thub, to be able, to be capable of)
glossary.ཐོབ་པ: thob pa — one who has gained (thob 'to get, to attain' + pa)
glossary.ཐོབ་པའི: thob pa'i — of gaining, that gains (thob pa 'to obtain' + -'i 'of'): grol ba thob pa'i 'of gaining freedom'
glossary.ཐོབ་པར: thob par — to attain, to obtain (thob pa + -r 'to'): thob par 'gyur 'will attain'
glossary.ཐོས་གྲོལ: thos grol — liberation through hearing (thos 'hear' + grol 'be freed'); the Tibetan name of this book
glossary.ཐོས་པ: thos pa — hearing, learning: what one has heard from teachers (thos 'to hear' + -pa): thos pa rgya mtsho 'learning like an ocean'
glossary.དག: dag — pure, correct · plural marker after de: de dag 'those, these' · plural marker after nouns too: sgom chen dag 'great meditators', gzhan dag 'others'
glossary.དགོས: dgos — must, need to, have to (dgos)
glossary.དགོས་པ: dgos pa — need, necessity (dgos pa 'to need' + -pa): mi dgos pa 'no need'
glossary.དགྲར: dgrar — as an enemy, into an enemy (dgra 'enemy' + -r 'as, into')
glossary.དང: dang — and; with · after a verb: 'as soon as' (brgyal bsangs pa dang 'as soon as the faint has cleared')
glossary.དངངས: dngangs — dread, to be terrified (dngangs, the print's spelling of sngangs 'be terrified')
glossary.དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པར: dpag tu med par — beyond measure, countlessly (dpag tu med pa 'immeasurable' + -r 'to')
glossary.དཔའ་བོ: dpa' bo — hero (dpa' bo; Sanskrit vīra): in the tantras the male companions of the sky-goer women
glossary.དབང་དུ: dbang du — into the power of, under the sway of (dbang 'power' + -du 'into'): dbang du 'gro 'fall into the power of'
glossary.དམ་ཚིག: dam tshig — vow, sacred bond (Sanskrit samaya)
glossary.དུས་སུ: dus su — at the time (dus + su 'at')
glossary.དེ: de — that; he, it. After a verb (also te, ste): 'and then'
glossary.དེ་ལྟར: de ltar — thus, in that way (de 'that' + ltar 'like')
glossary.དེ་ལྟར་རོ: de ltar ro — is thus, is so (de ltar 'thus' + the sentence-ending -ro)
glossary.དེས་ན: des na — so, therefore, in that case (des 'by that' + na 'if, when')
glossary.དོད་པ: dod pa — standing out, projecting (dod 'to stick out, protrude' + -pa): 'bur du dod pa 'standing out in relief', of carved or moulded images
glossary.ན: na — if, when (after the verb); also 'in, at' · to be ill, sickness (na, the verb of na ba): skye rga na 'chi 'birth, ageing, sickness and death'
glossary.ནང: nang — inside, within (nang): 'od kyi nang nas 'from within the light'
glossary.ནའང: na'ang — even if (na 'if' + 'ang 'even'): yin na'ang 'even if it is'
glossary.ནས: nas — from; after a verb: 'having done, and then'
glossary.ནི: ni — as for: marks the topic of the sentence
glossary.ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོ: phyag rgya chen po — Great Seal, mahāmudrā: the realisation of the mind's nature (phyag rgya 'seal' + chen po 'great')
glossary.ཕྱི་མ: phyi ma — later, next, the life to come (phyi ma): skye ba phyi ma 'a later birth'
glossary.ཕྱིར: phyir — outside, outward(?). The reading is uncertain; another print has dri med, 'stainless', here · here plainly 'out, outward' (phyi 'outside' + -r): phyir log 'turn back out', phyir thon 'come out' · back: phyir mi ldog go 'does not turn back' (phyir 'back' + ldog 'turn') · because, for the sake of (de'i phyir 'therefore', ci'i phyir 'why'; yod pa'i phyir 'because there is')
glossary.ཕྱིར་རོ: phyir ro — because, for this reason (phyir 'because' + the sentence-ending -ro)
glossary.ཕྱེད་པའི: phyed pa'i — of dividing, that makes a distinction (phyed, a spelling of phye, the past stem of 'byed 'to open, to separate', + -pa + -'i 'of'): bye brag phyed 'make the distinction'
glossary.བག་ཆགས: bag chags — habitual tendencies, the traces past actions leave in the mind (bag chags; Sanskrit vāsanā)
glossary.བཏབ་པ: btab pa — cast, done to, having cast (btab, past of 'debs 'cast', + -pa): gshe skur btab pa 'having reviled'
glossary.བཙུན་པ: btsun pa — disciplined, of good conduct, a monk (btsun pa 'venerable'): mi btsun pa 'undisciplined'
glossary.བཞིན་དུ: bzhin du — just as, like (bzhin 'like' + -du); after a verb 'while, as': sngar bzhin du 'as before'
glossary.བཞུགས་སོ: bzhugs so — is present, is here (bzhugs, respectful for 'to sit, to stay', + the sentence-ending -so)
glossary.བཟླས་པ: bzlas pa — recitation, having recited, said of mantras (bzlas, the past stem of zlo 'recite': zlo / bzlas / bzla / zlos, + -pa)
glossary.བར་དོ: bar do — the between: the interval between two states, above all between death and rebirth (bar 'between' + do 'two')
glossary.བར་དོར: bar dor — in the bardo (bar do + -r 'in, into') · as the bardo: the -r marks what a thing is recognised as (bar dor ngo shes 'recognise as the bardo')
glossary.བརྒྱལ་བ: brgyal ba — fainting, a swoon (brgyal 'to faint' + -ba)
glossary.བརྩོན: brtson — diligent, to make an effort (brtson)
glossary.བཤད་པའི: bshad pa'i — of explanation, that is explained (bshad, the past stem of 'chad 'explain', + -pa + -'i 'of')
glossary.བསུ་བ: bsu ba — meeting, welcoming, going out to meet someone (bsu 'to meet, welcome' + -ba); bsu ba la 'ongs 'come to meet'
glossary.བསྐྱེད་རྫོགས: bskyed rdzogs — generation and completion, the two stages of tantric meditation (bskyed 'generate' + rdzogs 'complete')
glossary.བསྒོམ་པའི: bsgom pa'i — of meditating, that meditates (bsgom, the future stem of sgom 'meditate', + -pa + -'i 'of')
glossary.བསྒོམ་པར: bsgom par — to meditate, meditating (bsgom, the future stem of sgom, + -pa + -r 'to'): ma bsgom par 'without meditating'
glossary.བསྒོམས་པ: bsgoms pa — meditated, having meditated (bsgoms, past of sgom 'meditate', + -pa)
glossary.བསྒྱུར: bsgyur — changed, transformed (bsgyur, the past and future stem of sgyur 'to change': sgyur / bsgyur / bsgyur / sgyur)
glossary.བསྒྲིམས: bsgrims — drawn together, concentrated (bsgrims, the past stem of sgrim 'to hold tight, to concentrate': sgrim / bsgrims / bsgrim / sgrims)
glossary.བསྟན་པ: bstan pa — teaching, showing (bstan, past of ston 'show', + pa)
glossary.བསྟན་པར: bstan par — to be shown, to show (bstan, the past and future stem of ston 'show', + -pa + -r 'to'): bstan par bya 'is to be shown'
glossary.བྱ: bya — is to be done; called (bya, future of byed 'do'): zhes bya 'is called' · with 'I' as the doer: 'I shall do' (bya, future of byed), as in ngo shes bya 'I shall recognise'
glossary.བྱས: byas — did, made, having done (byas, past of byed 'do')
glossary.བྱས་པ: byas pa — done, having done (byas, past of byed 'do', + -pa)
glossary.བྱིན་རླབས: byin rlabs — blessing, grace (byin 'splendour' + rlabs 'wave'): the power that comes from the buddhas
glossary.བྱུང: byung — came about, happened, occurred (byung, past of 'byung)
glossary.བྱེ་བྲག: bye brag — kind, sort, variety (bye brag): rol mo'i bye brag 'kinds of music' · distinction, difference: bye brag phyed 'make the distinction'
glossary.བྱོན་པ: byon pa — coming, having come, appearing (byon, respectful past of 'byon, + -pa)
glossary.བྲིས་པ: bris pa — drawn, painted (bris, past of 'bri 'draw', + -pa)
glossary.བྲོས་པས: bros pas — because it has fled (bros pa, past of 'bros 'run away', + -s)
glossary.མ: ma — not (before past and imperative verbs) · in a prohibition also before the present stem: ma byed cig 'do not do!' · mother (ma): ma dang bu 'mother and child'
glossary.མ་ཁད་དུ: ma khad du — as soon as, the moment that · on the point of, just before: dbugs chad ma khad du 'as the breath is about to stop'
glossary.མ་ཐག་ཏུ: ma thag tu — as soon as, immediately after (ma 'not' + thag 'distance' + -tu: 'with no interval'): after a verb
glossary.མ་རིག: ma rig — ignorance, not knowing (ma 'not' + rig 'know'; also ma rig pa; Sanskrit avidyā)
glossary.མཁན་པོ: mkhan po — abbot, master of a monastery (mkhan po)
glossary.མཁའ་འགྲོ: mkha' 'gro — sky-goer, ḍākinī (mkha' 'sky' + 'gro 'go'; also written mkha' 'gro ma, with the feminine -ma)
glossary.མཁའ་སྤྱོད་དུ: mkha' spyod du — to the Sky-Faring realm (mkha' spyod 'Sky-Faring' + -du 'to')
glossary.མཁས་པ: mkhas pa — learned, a scholar (mkhas pa 'learned')
glossary.མངོན་རྟོགས: mngon rtogs — clear realisation, the text describing a deity to be visualised (mngon 'clear' + rtogs 'realise')
glossary.མཆོད་བསྟོད: mchod bstod — offering and praise (mchod 'offering' + bstod 'praise')
glossary.མཐུན་པའི: mthun pa'i — agreeing, in harmony (mthun pa + -'i 'of')
glossary.མཐོ་རིས་སུ: mtho ris su — in the higher realms (mtho ris 'higher realm' + -su 'in')
glossary.མཐོང་བ: mthong ba — seeing (mthong 'see' + -ba): mthong ba tsam gyis 'by merely seeing'
glossary.མཚན་ཉིད: mtshan nyid — characteristic, defining mark; the study of the characteristics of things, philosophy (mtshan nyid)
glossary.མཚན་ཉིད་པ: mtshan nyid pa — philosopher, one versed in the characteristics (mtshan nyid + -pa)
glossary.མར: mar — down, downward (mar, the opposite of yar 'up'); of time, 'on, onward' · butter (mar), another word of the same spelling
glossary.མི: mi — not (before present and future verbs) · person, human being (mi): 'dris pa'i mi 'a person one has known'
glossary.མི་ཡུལ་དུ: mi yul du — in the human world, in the land of humans (mi 'person' + yul 'land' + -du 'in')
glossary.མེད་དོ: med do — there is not (med + the sentence-ending -do)
glossary.མེད་པ: med pa — without, not existing (med + pa)
glossary.མེད་པའི: med pa'i — that is without (med pa + -'i 'of')
glossary.མེད་པས: med pas — because there is not (med 'there is not' + -pas 'because')
glossary.མོས་པ: mos pa — devotion, trust, interest (mos pa)
glossary.ཙམ: tsam — just, only, about · as much as, so much that (tsam): mgo 'gas pa tsam 'so loud as to split the head'
glossary.ཙམ་དུ: tsam du — just so far, just to the point of (tsam + du)
glossary.ཚན་ཆེ: tshan che — strong, of great force (tshan che; read so) · great in number, prevailing
glossary.ཚུལ: tshul — manner, custom, way (tshul): tshul dang mi mthun pa 'out of keeping with custom'
glossary.ཞི་ཁྲོའི: zhi khro'i — of the peaceful and wrathful ones (zhi khro + -'i 'of')
glossary.ཞི་བའི: zhi ba'i — of the peaceful, peaceful (zhi ba 'peaceful' + -'i 'of')
glossary.ཞིང: zhing — and, while: links one verb to the next (zhing, the form used after a vowel and after ng, n, m, r, l, '; also cing, shing) · realm, field; a buddha-field (zhing, short for zhing khams): dag pa'i zhing 'pure realm'
glossary.ཞིབ་ཏུ: zhib tu — in detail, carefully (zhib 'fine, minute' + -tu)
glossary.ཞེ: zhe — so, thus (zhe, the form zhes takes before na after ng, n, m, r, l, ' and a vowel; ce na after g, d, b, she na after s): gang zhe na 'if one asks which', the way a list is opened
glossary.ཟད་པ: zad pa — running out, exhaustion (zad 'be used up' + -pa)
glossary.ཟིན: zin — seized, caught; held (zin, the intransitive verb beside 'dzin 'to hold'): ngos zin 'recognise'
glossary.ཟེར: zer — say, call (zer 'say, speak') · ray, ray of light (zer), as in 'od zer, and sgra 'od zer gsum 'sound, light and rays'

about: The first part of text ga, the bardo of the wrathful deities. After the seven days of the peaceful deities, each of them a narrow passage at which the dead were pointed out and many freed, the text explains why many still are not: beings are countless, their karma and habits strong, and the wheel of ignorance never runs down. Now the fifty-eight blazing blood-drinking wrathful deities dawn, which are the peaceful deities changed in form, and terror makes recognition harder, though it also holds the mind to one point, so that a little recognition frees. Learning does not help here: abbots who hold the monastic discipline and teachers of philosophy, who never took the secret mantra to heart or who disparaged it, do not recognise its deities and turn from them in hatred, which is why no relics or rainbow light appear when they die. A follower of the secret mantra, even the lowest, even of unseemly conduct, recognises the wrathful deities as his own yidam and is freed, and signs appear at his death; practitioners of middling ability and above are led to the Sky-Faring realm as their breath stops, with a clear sky, rainbow light, flowers, scent and music for signs. Great meditators of the Great Perfection and the Great Seal recognise the clear light at the moment of death and need no reading; those who recognise in the bardo of reality or of becoming attain the other two bodies, and others are born in the higher realms. The part closes with praise of the Great Liberation through Hearing as the teaching that frees by hearing alone, after which no being it has reached can go to the lower realms.
